prompt: Why is a mirrored second disk (RAID 1) not a backup?
hint: What happens on one disk happens on the other.

choices.text: The second disk is always empty until the first fails
choices.why: A mirror holds the same data all the time.

choices.text: A deletion or ransomware hits both at once
choices.why: Right. It protects against hardware failure, not against mistakes or attacks.

choices.text: RAID only works with cloud storage
choices.why: RAID is about disks in one machine.

choices.text: Mirrored disks are slower to read from
choices.why: Speed is not the issue.

prompt: Match each arrangement to what it does when somebody deletes the orders table.

pairs.left: a folder synchronised to the cloud
last night's backup, kept with retention

prompt: A file was corrupted a week ago, and the backup overwrites itself every night. What does the shop have?

choices.text: Only copies of the damaged version
choices.why: Right. Retention is what keeps the past.

choices.text: Nothing, since corruption deletes backups
choices.why: The backup is there; it is just wrong.

choices.text: A week of versions to choose from
choices.why: Overwriting keeps one version.

choices.text: A good copy from last night
choices.why: Last night copied the corrupted file.

prompt: What are the two halves of resilience, in the lesson's terms?

choices.text: Redundancy, then backups
choices.why: Right. Fast and copies damage; slow and keeps the past.

choices.text: Encryption and passwords
choices.why: Those protect confidentiality.

choices.text: A firewall and a DMZ
choices.why: Those are network segmentation.

choices.text: Prevention and detection
choices.why: Those are control functions from lesson 4.

prompt: Match each number of the 3-2-1 rule to what it means.
A backup disk stays plugged into the server all the time. Why does the modern rule want another copy too?
hint: What can ransomware on the server reach?

choices.text: The 3-2-1 rule forbids disks
choices.why: Disks are one of the media.

choices.text: It counts as the off-site copy already
choices.why: It is in the same building as the server.

choices.text: Whatever takes the server takes it
choices.why: Right. One copy offline or immutable.

choices.text: Plugged-in disks wear out faster
choices.why: Wear is not the argument.

prompt: A copy that nothing, not even an administrator, can change until a date has passed is called ___.
The shop encrypts its backups. Where should the key be kept?
hint: Not on the backup, not on the server.

choices.text: On the server, so the restore is automatic
choices.why: Ransomware takes it with the server.

choices.text: Away from both, with a backup of its own
choices.why: Right. Held by a person.

choices.text: On the backup disk, so the two are never separated
choices.why: Then the backup is readable by whoever takes the disk.

choices.text: Nowhere: encrypted backups need no key
choices.why: Without the key nothing is restorable.

choices.text: Which files to include
choices.why: Selection is a separate question.

choices.text: How fast the restore must be
choices.why: That is the RTO.

choices.text: How much the backup disk costs
choices.why: Cost follows the target; it does not define it.

choices.text: The frequency of backups
choices.why: Right. A nightly backup misses a target of one hour.

prompt: The shop backs up every night at 02:00. A disaster happens at 22:00 the same day. How many hours of orders are lost?
hint: From the last good backup to the disaster.

prompt: The website has an RPO of one week and an RTO of two hours. What does that combination say?

choices.text: The targets contradict each other
choices.why: They describe different things.

choices.text: Back up every two hours
choices.why: The RPO, not the RTO, sets the frequency.

choices.text: Old data is fine; downtime is not
choices.why: Right. Its data hardly changes and every hour offline loses sales.

choices.text: The site needs no backup at all
choices.why: A week's RPO still needs a backup.

prompt: Why does the lesson call an RTO a claim until it is tested?

choices.text: RTOs are set by auditors, not by the business
choices.why: The business decides them.

choices.text: RTOs change every day
choices.why: They change when the business decides.

choices.text: Nobody has timed a restore yet
choices.why: Right. Only a timed restore proves the number.

choices.text: Backups are never needed in practice
choices.why: This lesson exists because they are.

prompt: The backup job printed nothing when it ran. What did that mean?

choices.text: It needs a password to print anything
choices.why: No password is involved.

choices.text: It had failed silently
choices.why: It succeeded; that was the trap.

choices.text: It was still running in the background
choices.why: It had finished.

choices.text: Success, as written
choices.why: Right. It did exactly what its March version said.

prompt: diff -r printed Only in /srv/shop: invoices and exit 1. What had the restore test found?

choices.text: The invoices were corrupted on the server
choices.why: They exist on the server; they are missing from the restore.

choices.text: The archive was encrypted
choices.why: It extracted normally.

choices.text: A folder absent from the backup
choices.why: Right. The job had never been told about it.

choices.text: diff could not read the restore folder
choices.why: It read it and compared.

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer backing up everything minus exclusions over a list of what to include?

choices.text: A new folder is protected by default
choices.why: Right. Like default deny, turned around.

choices.text: Exclusion lists are shorter to type
choices.why: Length is not the reason.

choices.text: tar cannot read include lists
choices.why: It reads them; the job used one.

choices.text: Backups of everything are smaller
choices.why: They are larger, and that is the price.

prompt: What exit status did diff -r give once the restore matched the live data?
One byte of the off-site copy was overwritten. How did ana know?

choices.text: The file name ended in .bad
choices.why: Nothing renamed it.

choices.text: The copy's size changed
choices.why: dd overwrote a byte; the size stayed the same.

choices.text: tar refused to list it
choices.why: The lesson compared hashes, not tar output.

choices.text: Its hash differed
choices.why: Right. e8d08466 against 6342cb6d.

prompt: Order the shop's backup routine from the nightly step to the yearly one.
items: the job backs up everything under /srv/shop
a hash of the archive is recorded beside it
every copy is checked against the hash on arrival
a monthly restore into an empty folder, compared and timed
a yearly walk-through of restoring the whole shop
trap: A copy can only be checked against a hash recorded before it travelled.

prompt: Which of these protect against ransomware that controls the server? Choose all that apply.
hint: What can the server not reach?

choices.text: a folder synchronised from the server
choices.why: It syncs the encrypted files.

choices.text: cloud storage the server's credentials cannot change
choices.why: Immutable from the server's point of view.

choices.text: a disk unplugged and kept in a drawer
choices.why: Offline.

choices.text: a RAID mirror inside the server
choices.why: Encrypted along with the first disk.
